addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- dev: TDD Developer agent - implements features using test-driven development and clean code principles (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:design:design-implementation-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to verify that a UI implementation matches its Figma design specifications. This agent should be called after code has been written to implement a design, particularly after HTML/CSS/React components have been created or modified. The agent will visually compare the live implementation against the Figma design and provide detailed feedback on discrepancies.

Examples:
- <example>
  Context: The user has just implemented a new component based on a Figma design.
  user: "I've finished implementing the hero section based on the Figma design"
  assistant: "I'll review how well your implementation matches the Figma design."
  <commentary>
  Since UI implementation has been completed, use the design-implementation-reviewer agent to compare the live version with Figma.
  </commentary>
  </example>
- <example>
  Context: After the general code agent has implemented design changes.
  user: "Update the button styles to match the new design system"
  assistant: "I've updated the button styles. Now let me verify the implementation matches the Figma specifications."
  <commentary>
  After implementing design changes, proactively use the design-implementation-reviewer to ensure accuracy.
  </commentary>
  </example> (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:design:design-iterator: Use this agent PROACTIVELY when design work isn't coming together on the first attempt. If you've made 1-2 design changes and the result still feels off, suggest using this agent with 5x or 10x iterations for deeper refinement. This agent takes screenshots, analyzes what's not working, implements improvements, and repeats N times to systematically fix design issues. Perfect when colors feel wrong, layouts aren't balanced, or the overall aesthetic needs work that single changes can't achieve. <example>Context: User asks to change button color but result still looks off. user: "Change the button to blue" assistant: [makes change, takes screenshot] "The button is now blue, but I notice the overall color balance still feels off. Would you like me to use the design-iterator agent with 5 iterations to systematically improve the color harmony and visual balance?" <commentary>PROACTIVE USE: After a simple change doesn't fully resolve the design issue, suggest the design-iterator to do deeper work.</commentary></example> <example>Context: User's design request leads to something that doesn't look right. user: "Make the hero section more modern" assistant: [makes initial changes] "I've added some modern elements, but the result isn't quite coming together. This looks like it needs iterative refinement. Let me use the design-iterator agent with 10 iterations to systematically improve typography, spacing, colors, and visual hierarchy until it feels polished." <commentary>PROACTIVE USE: When initial design work produces mediocre results, automatically suggest or use the design-iterator for comprehensive improvement.</commentary></example> <example>Context: User wants explicit iterative refinement. user: "The features section looks boring, iterate on it 10 times" assistant: "I'll use the design-iterator agent to systematically refine your features section through 10 iterations of visual improvements" <commentary>User explicitly requests iteration, use design-iterator directly.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Design task requires research and multiple passes. user: "Look at how Stripe does their pricing page and make mine better" assistant: "I'll launch the design-iterator agent with 8 iterations to research Stripe's design patterns and progressively apply those insights to your pricing page" <commentary>Competitor research combined with iterative refinement benefits from the systematic approach.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:review:data-integrity-guardian: Use this agent when you need to review database migrations, data models, or any code that manipulates persistent data. This includes checking migration safety, validating data constraints, ensuring transaction boundaries are correct, and verifying that referential integrity and privacy requirements are maintained. <example>Context: The user has just written a database migration that adds a new column and updates existing records. user: "I've created a migration to add a status column to the orders table" assistant: "I'll use the data-integrity-guardian agent to review this migration for safety and data integrity concerns" <commentary>Since the user has created a database migration, use the data-integrity-guardian agent to ensure the migration is safe, handles existing data properly, and maintains referential integrity.</commentary></example> <example>Context: The user has implemented a service that transfers data between models. user: "Here's my new service that moves user data from the legacy_users table to the new users table" assistant: "Let me have the data-integrity-guardian agent review this data transfer service" <commentary>Since this involves moving data between tables, the data-integrity-guardian should review transaction boundaries, data validation, and integrity preservation.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:review:data-migration-expert: Use this agent when reviewing PRs that touch database migrations, data backfills, or any code that transforms production data. This agent validates ID mappings against production reality, checks for swapped values, verifies rollback safety, and ensures data integrity during schema changes. Essential for any migration that involves ID mappings, column renames, or data transformations. <example>Context: The user has a PR with database migrations that involve ID mappings. user: "Review this PR that migrates from action_id to action_module_name" assistant: "I'll use the data-migration-expert agent to validate the ID mappings and migration safety" <commentary>Since the PR involves ID mappings and data migration, use the data-migration-expert to verify the mappings match production and check for swapped values.</commentary></example> <example>Context: The user has a migration that transforms enum values. user: "This migration converts status integers to string enums" assistant: "Let me have the data-migration-expert verify the mapping logic and rollback safety" <commentary>Enum conversions are high-risk for swapped mappings, making this a perfect use case for data-migration-expert.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:review:deployment-verification-agent: Use this agent when a PR touches production data, migrations, or any behavior that could silently discard or duplicate records. Produces a concrete pre/post-deploy checklist with SQL verification queries, rollback procedures, and monitoring plans. Essential for risky data changes where you need a Go/No-Go decision. <example>Context: The user has a PR that modifies how emails are classified. user: "This PR changes the classification logic, can you create a deployment checklist?" assistant: "I'll use the deployment-verification-agent to create a Go/No-Go checklist with verification queries" <commentary>Since the PR affects production data behavior, use deployment-verification-agent to create concrete verification and rollback plans.</commentary></example> <example>Context: The user is deploying a migration that backfills data. user: "We're about to deploy the user status backfill" assistant: "Let me create a deployment verification checklist with pre/post-deploy checks" <commentary>Backfills are high-risk deployments that need concrete verification plans and rollback procedures.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools)

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## plugin:entire-engineering:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

{"additions":885,"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjM0ODEzMjc0","is_bot":false,"login":"MuskanPaliwal","name":"Muskan Paliwal"},"baseRefName":"main","body":"Fixes #2035.

Session-end condensation could make a checkpoint durable before its updated session state was saved. If the hook was killed in that window, recovery still considered the transcript unfinished and could write it again under a different checkpoint ID.

On current `main`, the immediate `PostCommit` path described in the issue no longer reproduces this for a no-files session because that path discards it. The durable failure still reproduces through `entire doctor`, which sees the ended session as unfinished and previously generated a new checkpoint ID for the same transcript range.

### Approach

This PR uses a write-ahead checkpoint ID. It saves the intended ID as `CondensationAttemptID`, writes the checkpoint with that ID, advances the session bookkeeping, and then clears the pending attempt. If the process dies after the write, the next attempt reuses the same ID instead of creating a duplicate.

The reservation is also honored during commit preparation and `PostCommit`. If `PostCommit` receives a different checkpoint ID, it preserves the interrupted session and shadow branch rather than overwriting its recovery state.

Advancing `LastCheckpointID` or `CheckpointTranscriptStart` before writing would prevent duplication but introduce a data-loss window: state could claim that a transcript was saved when the checkpoint write had failed. The pending ID records durable intent without claiming that the write succeeded.

`CondensationRecoveryPending` separately records when recovery may need to reconcile an interrupted write created by an older CLI version. This keeps the more expensive storage lookup out of normal condensation paths.

Reserved writes are routed using their checkpoint ID format. If checkpoint configuration changes between reservation and retry, the checkpoint is still written to the backend that originally generated its ID.

### Recovering state from older CLI versions

Older interrupted sessions have no pending checkpoint ID. Doctor reconciles them using the session identity, transcript bounds and content, checkpoint counts, agent and turn metadata, touched files, and session kind. Externalized images are reinserted before comparing transcripts.

Storage listing or reading failures stop recovery and preserve its state for another retry rather than being treated as “checkpoint not found.” If the session has genuinely advanced, recovery creates a new checkpoint instead of reusing the older one.

### Related findings

`checkpoint list` exposes both duplicates because they have different checkpoint IDs, while `tokens profile` can count both and inflate checkpoint-observed token totals. The latter already warns about overlapping checkpoint history.

Codex kills timed-out hook process groups with `SIGKILL`, not `SIGTERM`, so Entire cannot print its normal termination message during a Codex timeout. See Codex’s [hook runner](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/bb701f1e8c8db884fa0cdafff4b8dcb1604f2fdd/codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs) and [process-group cleanup](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/bb701f1e8c8db884fa0cdafff4b8dcb1604f2fdd/codex-rs/utils/pty/src/process_group.rs).

### Follow-up plan

This PR lands the non-destructive part first: it prevents new duplicate checkpoints, makes retries deterministic, and reconciles interrupted writes from older CLI versions. It deliberately does not remove or hide duplicate pairs that already exist.

Questions for a follow-up:

### Approach

This PR uses a write-ahead checkpoint ID. It saves the intended ID as `CondensationAttemptID`, writes the checkpoint with that ID, advances the session bookkeeping, and then clears the pending attempt. If the process dies after the write, the next attempt reuses the same ID instead of creating a duplicate.

The reservation is also honored during commit preparation and `PostCommit`. If `PostCommit` receives a different checkpoint ID, it preserves the interrupted session and shadow branch rather than overwriting its recovery state.

package strategy

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// Proves recoverInterruptedCondensation redirects the checkpoint ID away from
// the caller-supplied one, even when the caller is PostCommit and that ID came
// from an already-written commit trailer.
func TestProbe_RecoveryRedirectsCheckpointIDAwayFromCallerID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := OpenRepository(context.Background())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer repo.Close()

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "probe-recovery-redirect"
	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)

	st, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	endedAt := time.Now().UTC()
	st.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
	st.EndedAt = &endedAt
	st.FilesTouched = nil
	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), st))

	// 1. A legacy orphan checkpoint L exists (interrupted write, state not advanced).
	stale, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	orphanID := id.MustCheckpointID("111111111111")
	res, err := s.CondenseSession(context.Background(), repo, orphanID, stale, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.False(t, res.Skipped)

	// 2. Doctor reserved D and set RecoveryPending, then died before condensing.
	trailerID := id.MustCheckpointID("222222222222")
	require.NoError(t, MutateSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID, func(state *SessionState) error {
		state.CondensationAttemptID = trailerID
		state.CondensationRecoveryPending = true
		return nil
	}))

	// 3. A commit now carries trailer D; PostCommit condenses with checkpointID = D.
	postCommitState, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	result, err := s.CondenseSession(context.Background(), repo, trailerID, postCommitState, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.False(t, result.Skipped)

	// condenseAndUpdateState assigns state.LastCheckpointID = result.CheckpointID
	assert.Equal(t, orphanID, result.CheckpointID,
		"recovery redirected the write to the orphan")
	assert.NotEqual(t, trailerID, result.CheckpointID,
		"the commit trailer ID is NOT what got written")

	// And no checkpoint exists under the trailer ID the commit points at.
	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo, checkpoint.DefaultV1Refs())
	summary, err := store.Read(context.Background(), trailerID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Nil(t, summary, "commit trailer points at a checkpoint that was never written")
}
EOF

content.text:
I read the whole diff, built it, ran the touched packages' tests (green), and probed the one path I was unsure about. Muskan's comment is just a review request, so here's the review.

## Verdict

The core idea is right — a write-ahead checkpoint ID, with the explicit choice *not* to advance `LastCheckpointID`/`CheckpointTranscriptStart` first, is the correct trade and the PR body argues it well. Reserve-before-write is genuinely two separate persisted `MutateSessionState` calls in both entry points, so the window really is closed. All three `WriteRequest` dispatch sites are updated (grepped — no store left to silently reject the new type).

Two things should block merge, both about what happens *after* reservation.

---

### 1. Legacy recovery redirects the checkpoint ID on the PostCommit path → dangling commit trailer

`manual_commit_condensation.go:365` runs `recoverInterruptedCondensation` on `state.CondensationRecoveryPending` with **no restriction on the caller**. When it hits, it returns a *different* `CheckpointID`. On the PostCommit path the commit trailer is already written, so:

- `manual_commit_hooks.go:1442` → `state.LastCheckpointID = result.CheckpointID` (the orphan)
- the commit still says `Entire-Checkpoint: <trailer ID>`
- `updateCombinedAttributionForCheckpoint(ctx, repo, checkpointID, …)` writes attribution under the trailer ID

So the commit points at a checkpoint that was never written. Verified with a throwaway test (removed):

```
INFO recovered interrupted condensation checkpoint_id=111111111111
--- PASS  (result.CheckpointID == orphan, trailer 222222222222 reads back nil)
```

This isn't only reachable via SIGKILL. `CondenseSessionByID` persists `CondensationRecoveryPending = true` in mutate #1; if mutate #2's condense returns an error, doctor prints `Warning: failed to condense session …` (`doctor.go:193`) and moves on — **the flag stays set forever**, so every subsequent commit for that session enters recovery.

Fix: gate recovery on the caller, e.g. a `condenseOpts` flag set only by the doctor/eager paths. PostCommit's ID comes from the trailer, which is already durable — it never needs recovery.

### 2. The new PostCommit guard removes PostCommit as the retry path, and the fast path can't feed it

`manual_commit_hooks.go:1203` early-returns whenever `CondensationAttemptID != checkpointID`, skipping the entire `EventGitCommit` transition. But `addTrailerForAgentCommit` calls `checkpointIDForSessions(logCtx, []*SessionState{state})` (`:2132`) with only the single ACTIVE session `tryAgentCommitFastPath` picked — an ENDED session holding a reserved ID never contributes. So every agent (no-TTY) commit mints a fresh ID and skips the interrupted session again, indefinitely.

Recovery then needs interactive `entire doctor` — `entire status`'s exited-owner sweep excludes ENDED sessions. Before this PR PostCommit condensed it (duplicating); now it's stuck until a human intervenes. Same shape when two sessions hold distinct reserved IDs.

Fix is small: pass the full `sessions` slice in the fast path. `checkpointIDForSessions` already takes a slice and does exactly the right thing.

---

### Should fix

**3. `CondensationRecoveryPending` leaks a doctor-only, fail-closed scan into the commit hook.** `findInterruptedCondensation` does `store.List` across both backends plus `Read` + `ReadSessionMetadata` per matching checkpoint, and aborts on the *first* read failure — including `ErrCheckpointNotFound` on a listed-but-unreadable checkpoint. Because the flag persists (see #1), one unreadable checkpoint permanently blocks condensation for that session. The intent is right; scope the blast radius: don't abort the search on an unrelated candidate, and fall through to a fresh write rather than never condensing.

**4. `ReservedSession` on every condensation write misroutes fresh checkpoints.** `condensationSessionWriteRequest` returns `ReservedSession` unconditionally, but `GenerateCheckpointID` (`generate.go:19`) falls back to hex when `LoadCheckpointsConfig` errors — documented fail-soft. Under a git-refs primary that fresh hex ID takes the mismatch branch in `writeReservedSession` and lands on the **git-branch** store, bypassing the configured primary and every mirror. The PR's own `TestKindRoutingStore_ReservedSessionUsesOriginalBackendAfterConfigChange/hex reserved under branch after switching to refs` encodes that behaviour, and it contradicts `routing_store.go:26` ("Fresh creates … go to the configured primary (+ mirrors)"). Emit `ReservedSession` only when `state.CondensationAttemptID == checkpointID`.

### Minor

- `routing_store.go:258` — a `readTarget.Read` error fails the write, but `firstResolved` already falls through on a non-final store's error, so the branch-only write stays readable. Log and proceed.
- `routing_store.go:247` — if `primaryType` is neither `git-branch` nor `git-refs`, `targetType == s.primaryType` is never true, so *every* reserved write bypasses `s.writer`. `readOrder` has an explicit `default:` for that case; mirror it.
- The refactor dropped `// Post-commit emits regex-only blobs. OPF runs later in the pre-push rewrite path, never here.` with no replacement. That's a load-bearing guardrail — put it on `buildCondensationWriteOptions`.
- `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` now carries two copies of the FilesTouched / StepCount / shadow-branch skip ladder that must stay in sync. Extract a predicate.
- Perf: the reservation adds a third `MutateSessionState` inside the Codex session-end deadline, and flock acquire blocks. `markSessionEnded` (`lifecycle.go:1561`) is already a mutate on the same state — reserving there is free.
- The `lifecycle.go` doc rewrite drops "PostCommit retries". Given #2 that's no longer true when the IDs differ; say doctor.

### On the four follow-up questions

(1) Collapse in `checkpoint list`/`tokens profile`, don't rewrite history — the v1 branch is pushed and shared. (2) The later recovery write, since it's the one whose metadata matches current state. (3) Reporting-only in `doctor` first. (4) Keep it scoped to session-end + doctor; a global transcript-range rule puts a storage scan on the hot commit path, which is the same mistake as #3 above.

---

Findings 1 and 2 are the ones I'd hold on. Want me to post this as a PR comment?

Note: this worktree is now checked out at `pr-2038` (was `soph/review-2038`).

package strategy

// Two sessions in one worktree: A is ENDED holding a reserved attempt ID from an
// interrupted eager condense; B is ACTIVE (an agent about to commit). Does the
// commit trailer carry A's reserved ID, or a fresh one?
func TestProbe_AgentFastPathIgnoresOtherSessionsReservedID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := OpenRepository(context.Background())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer repo.Close()

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	// Session A: ENDED, no files, reserved attempt ID (interrupted condense).
	sessionA := "interrupted-ended-session"
	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionA)
	reservedID := id.MustCheckpointID("111111111111")
	require.NoError(t, MutateSessionState(context.Background(), sessionA, func(st *SessionState) error {
		endedAt := time.Now().UTC()
		st.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
		st.EndedAt = &endedAt
		st.FilesTouched = nil
		st.CondensationAttemptID = reservedID
		return nil
	}))

	// Session B: ACTIVE agent session with its own work.
	sessionB := "active-agent-session"
	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionB)
	require.NoError(t, s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), sessionB, agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, "", "startup", ""))

	stB, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionB)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, session.PhaseActive, stB.Phase)

	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(dir, "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte("agent commit\n"), 0o600))
	require.NoError(t, s.PrepareCommitMsg(context.Background(), commitMsgFile, "message"))

	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	got, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	require.True(t, found, "expected a checkpoint trailer")
	t.Logf("trailer=%s reservedA=%s", got, reservedID)
	assert.Equal(t, reservedID, got,
		"trailer should carry A's reserved ID, else PostCommit's guard skips A")
}
EOF

content.text:
## Short answer

No integration tests, no e2e. `git diff main...pr-2038 --stat -- cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/ e2e/` is empty — everything is unit tests in `strategy` and `checkpoint`. The fixed flow *is* replicated, but only in-process.

## What's actually covered, and covered well

These are real regression tests, not smoke tests:

- `TestCondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed_ReusesReservedAttemptAfterInterruptedWrite` — reserves the ID, writes the checkpoint out-of-band against a deliberately stale state (a faithful in-process stand-in for "SIGKILLed after the durable write"), re-enters the eager path, asserts `Len(checkpoints, 1)` + ID match + attempt cleared. This is the actual bug, tested.
- `TestCondenseSessionByID_ReusesCheckpointFromInterruptedEagerCondense` — the legacy no-reserved-ID reconciliation, same one-checkpoint assertion.
- `TestCondenseSessionByID_DoesNotReuseCheckpointAfterSessionAdvances` — the negative case (genuinely advanced session → 2 checkpoints). This is the one people usually skip; good that it's here.
- `TestFindInterruptedCondensation_PropagatesIndeterminateReadErrors` — table across all four read stages.
- `TestKindRoutingStore_ReservedSessionRetryUpdatesBothBackendsOnce` — asserts the branch tip gained exactly one commit by comparing parent hashes, i.e. proves the mirror fan-out didn't double-write. Genuinely good test.

Statement coverage on the new code: `postCommitProcessSessionLocked` 98%, `recoverInterruptedCondensation` 90%, `findInterruptedCondensation` 83%, `writeReservedSession` 82%, `CondenseSessionByID` 75%, `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` 73%.

## Gaps, ranked

**1. No integration test, though the harness already has every piece.** Integration hooks run the real binary as subprocesses — the only place the reservation's two-`MutateSessionState` ordering, the flock acquire, and the session-end deadline get exercised for real. `TestEnv` already exposes `SimulateSessionEnd` (eager condense), `GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent` (the fast path), `RunCLI` (so `entire doctor --force`), `GetSessionState`, `GetLatestCheckpointID`, `AssertCheckpointContainsSession`. `integration_test/fully_condensed_test.go` is the template. The missing test is ~40 lines: end session → assert one checkpoint → forge the interrupted state (un-advance `CheckpointTranscriptStart`/`StepCount`/`FullyCondensed`, keep `CondensationAttemptID`) → commit *and* `entire doctor --force` → assert still one checkpoint.

**2. `entire doctor` is never run.** The PR body names doctor as the reproduction ("The durable failure still reproduces through `entire doctor`"), but the tests call `CondenseSessionByID` directly. That skips doctor's stuck-session detection, the `HasShadowBranch && CheckpointCount > 0` gate at `doctor.go:192`, and the condense-vs-discard branch. The stated repro has no test.

**3. `transcriptForRecoveryComparison` is 25% — the reinjection body is zero-covered.** Only the `codec == nil || len(assets) == 0` early return executes; lines 25–40 (the `byName` map and `ReinjectImages` call) never run, because every recovery test passes `nil` assets. The PR description advertises "Externalized images are reinserted before comparing transcripts" as part of the design, and it's a byte-equality comparison — if `ReinjectImages` doesn't reproduce the pre-externalization bytes exactly, recovery silently misses and you get the duplicate anyway, with no test to notice. `image_externalize_test.go` / `codex_image_externalize_test.go` are the models; a unit test with one Claude Code image asset would be cheap.

**4. Multi-session cases are untested — and that's exactly where finding #2 lives.** `checkpointIDForSessions` is only ever called with a one-element slice in tests, despite taking a slice precisely so it can scan several. I wrote the missing case; it fails on this branch:

```
trailer=33d8b81c1705  reservedA=111111111111
```

ENDED session A holds reserved `111111111111`, ACTIVE session B commits via the agent fast path, trailer is fresh → PostCommit's new guard skips A. A test at that level catches it.

**5. Untested branches worth one test each:** the `CondenseSessionByID` `ErrMutationSkip` guard (`CondensationAttemptID != checkpointID` — the concurrent-clear race between the two mutates), and `writeReservedSession`'s two error paths (fatal `readTarget.Read`, non-branch/refs primary) which are the uncovered 18%.

Both probe tests I used for this review are throwaway (removed, tree is clean), but both are worth landing as real tests — the second one as a failing test that #2's fix makes pass. Happy to write the integration test and the image-asset recovery test if useful.

content.text:
Mostly, yes — five of the nine findings become tests. Four don't, and there's a mechanics problem with "stacked".

## What tests can and can't prove

| Finding | Provable by test? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Recovery redirects ID on PostCommit → dangling trailer | **Yes** | integration (commit → assert trailer resolves) + the unit probe I ran |
| 2. Fast path never offers the reserved ID → starvation | **Yes** | unit probe I ran; integration via `GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent` |
| 3a. One unreadable checkpoint permanently blocks condensation | **Yes** | unit, fake store |
| 3b. `store.List` + per-checkpoint reads on every commit | Benchmark only | `integration_test/hook_bench_test.go` exists |
| 4. Fresh writes misrouted under fail-soft config read | **Yes** | unit, `checkpoint` pkg |
| 5. `writeReservedSession` fatal read error / non-git primary bypass | **Yes** | unit |
| 6. Dropped OPF invariant comment | No | review comment |
| 7. Duplicated skip ladder in `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` | No | refactor; `dupl`@75 won't catch it |
| 8. Extra flock round-trip inside the Codex session-end budget | No | design |
| 9. `lifecycle.go` doc now overclaims | No | comment |

Two caveats on the ones that *are* testable:

- **#3 is a policy disagreement, not a bug.** The PR deliberately chose fail-closed ("Storage listing or reading failures stop recovery … rather than being treated as 'checkpoint not found'"). A failing test there just encodes our preference as red CI. Worth settling in conversation first; the *consequence* (permanently blocked condensation) is the part to demonstrate.
- **"Proving it works in general" should include the negative direction**, or it only proves dedup: a genuinely-advanced session still gets a *new* checkpoint, and an ordinary single-session flow produces byte-identical results to main (same checkpoint count, mirrors still written). Otherwise the integration suite can't distinguish "fixed" from "now dedupes too aggressively".

## The stacking problem

#2038 is from a fork — `MuskanPaliwal:fix-session-end-checkpoint-duplication`. GitHub won't let us open a PR in `entireio/cli` based on a fork branch, so a true stack in our repo isn't available. `maintainer_can_modify` is `true`, which opens up other shapes.

And `test:ci` is a single `go test -tags=integration -race ./...`, so one intentionally-red test reds the whole run and blocks #2038 from merging.

options.label: Hand her a patch, no PR
options.description: Produce the tests as a patch/diff in a PR comment for her to apply. Lowest friction, no CI signal, easiest for her to ignore.

questions.question: What should the failing tests do to CI?

options.label: Tests + fixes together (Recommended)
options.description: Each finding gets its failing test and its fix in the same branch, one commit pair each. Red→green is visible per commit, the tip is green, nothing blocks #2038 from merging.

options.label: Red tests as the spec
options.description: Land only the failing tests and let CI stay red until the findings are addressed. Unambiguous about what's broken, but blocks #2038 and reds every unrelated PR that rebases onto it.

options.label: Failing tests skipped with a reason
options.description: t.Skip with the finding written out and a link. CI stays green, the bug is documented in code, but nothing enforces it and skips rot quietly.

options.label: Green proof now, findings as comments
options.description: Stacked PR carries only the passing integration suite; the nine findings stay as review comments on #2038. Smallest change, but the two blockers have no executable proof.
